label: How the fidel works
desc: One consonant in seven vowel orders, using በ ቡ ቢ ባ ቤ ብ ቦ, and how to read a syllable

label: Fidel rows: ሀ to ቸ
desc: The rows ሀ ለ ሐ መ ሠ ረ ሰ ሸ ቀ በ ቨ ተ ቸ, including ቀ as an ejective

label: Fidel rows: ኀ to ዠ
desc: The rows ኀ ነ ኘ አ ከ ኸ ወ ዐ ዘ ዠ

label: Fidel rows: የ to ፐ
desc: The rows የ ደ ጀ ገ ጠ ጨ ጰ ጸ ፀ ፈ ፐ, with the ejectives ጠ ጨ ጰ ጸ

label: Reading words
desc: Letters that sound the same, the -wa forms, and short words. The fidel does not mark gemination; the romanisation line doubles the long consonant

label: Greetings and courtesy
desc: ሰላም, ጤና ይስጥልኝ, time-of-day greetings for a man, a woman and እርስዎ, and please

label: About me
desc: Name, origin and the pronoun set with ነኝ ነህ ነሽ ነው ናት

label: People and family
desc: Family words and the possessive endings, with the man and woman forms kept apart

label: Numbers, time and prices
desc: Numbers, ስንት ሰዓት ነው, Ethiopian clock examples from the Peace Corps manual, and prices in ብር

label: Classroom and home
desc: This and that, the definite ending, plurals in -ኦች, and አለኝ / የለኝም

label: Food and drink
desc: Restaurant food and drinks from the Peace Corps menu, እንጀራ, ቡና, ውሃ, and the bill

label: Likes and free time
desc: Wanting with the infinitive, and likes and dislikes

label: Getting around
desc: በ- ከ- ለ- ወደ, left and right, and where a place is

label: Verbs
desc: Perfective and imperfective person endings, and the object -ን

label: Questions and connectors
desc: ምን ማን የት መቼ ስንት እንዴት, and the small words that join clauses

label: Compliments
desc: Kind remarks about food, work, skills and people, using words attested in the opened sources, and a reply once one is checked

label: Traps for English speakers
desc: One you for everyone, a missing object -ን, a missing ነው, ejectives said as plain consonants, and gemination said short

label: Flirting
desc: Warm, respectful compliments for adults, the coffee invitation, a playful ኧረ, a warm yes and kind clear ways to say no, with man, woman and polite forms

label: Top nouns
desc: Everyday nouns not yet on another card: day, hour, woman, man, money, door, car, food words

label: Top verbs
desc: The verbs a beginner says most, in the form used: ነው, አለ, commands for a man, a woman and politely, and drink, eat, like, take

label: Top adjectives
desc: Big, small, many, fine, kind, expensive, red, far, cool, and the nationality words with their woman forms

label: Top pronouns
desc: Subject pronouns, the polite he or she, what, this, and the possessive endings shown on ስም and ልጅ

label: Top prepositions and postpositions
desc: The prefixes ከ- በ- ለ- joined to a word, the separate ወደ, and ጋር after the word

label: Top words
desc: Yes, no, OK, sorry, today, tomorrow, yesterday, three weekdays, and the teen and forty numbers
